detailed_rationale: [DATA] FY26 (ended 31-Mar-2026): consolidated AUM Rs.59,908cr, +16.4% YoY; Q4FY26 disbursements Rs.8,051cr, +17% YoY; FY26 disbursements Rs.32,321cr. Asset quality best-in-class and IMPROVING: gross Stage-3 stable at 1.44%, net Stage-3 down to 0.69% (vs 0.75% a year ago), provision cover up to 53%. NII +21% to Rs.3,376cr FY26; calc. NIM flat QoQ at 5.61%. Cost-to-income improved to 28.71% (vs 30.80% FY25) - best-in-class for the space. Standalone FY26 PAT +19% YoY to Rs.1,834cr; but Q4FY26 standalone PAT alone was almost flat YoY (Rs.554cr vs ~Rs.550cr, +0.2-0.7% depending on source) as employee costs (+18.4% YoY) and interest costs (+8.4% YoY) outran the 13.3% revenue growth - operating margin ex-other-income compressed ~494bps YoY in the quarter. [INFERENCE] the Q4-vs-FY26 divergence (19% full-year vs flat Q4) most likely reflects a strong Q4FY25 base (subsidiary-dividend timing is a common driver for this NBFC's Q4 prints) rather than a new one-off in the current quarter - sources did not disclose the exact dividend-income bridge, flagging as the one unresolved item. Consolidated (incl. Sundaram AMC, Sundaram Home Finance, Royal Sundaram General Insurance) FY26 net profit Rs.2,059cr, EPS Rs.185.32, well above standalone, confirming meaningful subsidiary uplift (SOTP-relevant) though granular subsidiary P&L wasn't available in the sources checked. Sundaram Home Finance disbursement/origination growth ~15% YoY (Mar-26) - healthy. [DATA] Valuation: CMP ~Rs.4,440, mkt cap ~Rs.49,362cr, P/E ~23.4x, P/B ~3.31x, ROE 15.0%, ROCE 9.44%. Reverse-check: P/B=(ROE-g)/(CoE-g) with ROE 15%, CoE~13% implies market is pricing ~12% sustained growth in equity/earnings - broadly consistent with the mid-teens AUM growth actually being delivered, i.e. the premium P/B is not obviously stretched on a pure lending-book basis, but it also isn't cheap - it embeds continuation of the current growth+asset-quality combo plus an implicit (unquantified) SOTP credit for the AMC/insurance/home-finance stack. No promoter/CEO regulatory-approval overhang or governance flag surfaced in this scan. Q1FY27 (Jun-2026 qtr) results not yet out as of 20-Jul-2026; typically reported within 45 days of quarter-end, so expected early-to-mid August 2026 (exact board-meeting date not yet disclosed in sources checked).
recommendation_rationale: No quant score exists yet for SUNDARMFIN in STOCK_SCORECARD_750 - per V1 rule this defaults to Hold absent an escalation-worthy red flag. Fundamentals support that default on their own merits: asset quality is improving (not deteriorating), NIM stable, cost ratios best-in-class, and full-year growth healthy (+19% standalone PAT, +16.4% AUM). The one soft spot - flat Q4 standalone profit on rising opex/funding cost - is a margin-pressure data point worth monitoring next quarter, not a thesis-breaking asset-quality or governance issue, so it does not rise to an escalation-worthy Sell. Valuation is rich (3.31x P/B, FAIR grade per one source) but the reverse-DCF check shows the premium is roughly explained by realistic mid-teens forward growth rather than requiring heroic assumptions, and part of the premium is legitimately subsidiary (AMC/insurance) SOTP value not on this note's checklist to quantify.
summary: Sundaram Finance closed FY26 with AUM +16.4% to Rs.59,908cr, best-in-class asset quality (net Stage-3 improved to 0.69%) and cost ratios (28.71% C/I), but Q4FY26 standalone profit growth stalled (~flat YoY) as employee and funding costs ran ahead of revenue growth for the quarter even as the full year posted +19% PAT growth. Valuation is premium (3.31x P/B, 23.4x P/E) but roughly justified by the growth being delivered; no regulatory or governance overhang identified. Q1FY27 results not yet released as of 20-Jul-2026.
positive_para: [DATA] Asset quality trend is genuinely improving, not just stable - net Stage-3 down to 0.69% from 0.75% YoY with provision cover rising to 53%, a rare positive direction in a vehicle-finance book growing AUM at mid-teens rates. Cost-to-income at 28.71% (best-in-class for the NBFC space) and NIM holding flat at 5.61% show funding-cost and opex discipline hasn't broken despite scale-up. Full-year FY26 standalone PAT grew a strong 19% and consolidated EPS (Rs.185.32) sits well above standalone, confirming the AMC/home-finance/general-insurance subsidiary stack is adding real earnings power beyond the core lending book - the classic Sundaram SOTP argument. Disbursements (+17% Q4, AUM +16.4% FY26) show no signs of a CV/tractor-cycle slowdown reaching this franchise yet, and no promoter, CEO-approval, or governance red flag surfaced in this scan.
negative_para: [DATA]/[INFERENCE] Q4FY26 standalone profit growth essentially stalled (near-flat YoY) as employee costs (+18.4%) and interest costs (+8.4%) outpaced 13.3% revenue growth, compressing the operating margin ~494bps YoY in the quarter - a genuine margin-pressure data point even if the full year still grew 19%; the exact driver of the sharp Q4-vs-FY26 divergence (likely a high Q4FY25 dividend-income base) was not confirmed in sources checked, so it remains an open item rather than a resolved one-off. Valuation is unambiguously premium at 3.31x P/B and 23.4x P/E for a lending business with ROE of only 15% (ROCE just 9.44%), leaving little room for a growth disappointment before a re-rating risk emerges. One source flagged recent share-price underperformance versus NBFC peers and negative one-year returns, which - while not a fundamental call - suggests the market may already be pricing in some of the Q4 margin-pressure signal ahead of full disclosure.
reverse_dcf_judgment: [INFERENCE] At P/B 3.31x and ROE 15% with an assumed cost of equity ~13%, the Gordon-growth back-solve (P/B=(ROE-g)/(CoE-g)) implies the market is pricing roughly 12% sustained forward growth in equity/earnings for the standalone lending business - which is broadly in line with the mid-teens AUM/disbursement growth actually being delivered (16.4%/17%). So the premium P/B is not obviously stretched on lending-book fundamentals alone; it is rich but roughly growth-justified, with additional (unquantified) upside/downside from the AMC + Royal Sundaram General Insurance + home-finance SOTP not captured in this simple check.

technical_commentary: One of the cleanest uptrends in the batch — an uninterrupted higher-low sequence since 2022 (1,555→2,206→2,493→3,733→3,925→4,200) and higher highs culminating in a fresh all-time high as recently as March 2026. The current -21% pullback is orderly and holds above the 40m average.
